title: Electronic Control Board Failure
shortDescription: The cooktop control board has detected an internal fault.
fullDescription:
F1 on a Frigidaire induction or electric cooktop indicates an internal electronic control board error. The board cannot validate its firmware or has detected an unrecoverable fault.

Power cycling sometimes clears transient faults; persistent F1 requires board replacement.

fixSteps.title: Reset power
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off at the breaker for 5 minutes.

whenToCallPro: Recommended because the cooktop runs on 240V.
videoSearchQuery: Frigidaire cooktop F1 control board fix

faq.a: No — the entire unit is disabled.

title: Over-Temperature Detected
shortDescription: Cooktop surface temperature has exceeded safe limits.
fullDescription:
F2 indicates an over-temperature condition — typically from an empty pan, poor heat transfer, or a failed surface temperature sensor.

The control shuts down the affected element to prevent damage to the glass or internal components.

fixSteps.title: Cool down
fixSteps.instruction: Remove cookware and let cooktop cool for 30 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Swap in a new surface temperature sensor.

whenToCallPro: If thermal damage to the glass is suspected.

faq.a: Usually no; the shutdown is protective.

title: Shorted Temperature Sensor
shortDescription: A surface temperature sensor has shorted.
fullDescription:
F3 indicates a shorted temperature sensor — the control board reads an impossibly low resistance.

The affected element is disabled until the sensor is replaced.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Look for visible damage to sensor wiring.

whenToCallPro: If disassembly of glass cooktop is uncomfortable.
videoSearchQuery: Frigidaire cooktop F3 sensor short fix

faq.a: Usually yes — only the affected zone is disabled.

title: Touch Control Failure
shortDescription: The touch control surface is not responding correctly.
fullDescription:
F5 signals stuck or shorted capacitive touch controls. Usually caused by spilled liquid, grease, or a failed touch module.

Clean the surface and reset; persistent errors require module replacement.

causes.cause: Liquid or debris on touch area

fixSteps.title: Clean surface
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe the touch area with a dry cloth.

videoSearchQuery: Frigidaire cooktop F5 touch error fix

faq.a: Usually a spill under the glass edge.

title: Line Voltage Error
shortDescription: Supply voltage is out of specification.
fullDescription:
F6 indicates the 240V supply is too high, too low, or unstable. The control protects the cooktop by halting operation.

Verify household voltage and breaker connections; persistent issues need an electrician.

fixSteps.title: Call electrician
fixSteps.instruction: If voltage is out of spec, request service.

whenToCallPro: Call an electrician if voltage issues persist.

faq.a: An electrician should verify the panel.

title: Cooling Fan Failure
shortDescription: The internal cooling fan is not running.
fullDescription:
F7 indicates the cooling fan that protects induction power modules is not spinning at the expected RPM. Without airflow, the power electronics will overheat.

Replace the fan motor or clear obstructions.

fixSteps.title: Clear intake
fixSteps.instruction: Vacuum dust from the fan intake grille.

whenToCallPro: Recommended for induction cooktops due to complex wiring.
videoSearchQuery: Frigidaire cooktop F7 cooling fan fix

faq.q: Why does it need a fan?
faq.a: Induction power modules dissipate significant heat.

title: Induction Module Communication Error
shortDescription: Communication with an induction module has failed.
fullDescription:
F8 indicates the main control cannot communicate with one of the induction power modules. This is specific to induction cooktops and halts the affected element.

Causes include loose ribbon cables or a failed power module.

fixSteps.title: Reseat cables
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect power and reseat ribbon connectors.

fixSteps.title: Replace module
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new induction power module.

faq.a: Yes — radiant cooktops will not show F8.

title: Pan Detection Error
shortDescription: Induction cooktop cannot detect compatible cookware.
fullDescription:
F9 occurs on induction cooktops when the element detects no pan or a non-magnetic pan. The zone cannot energize.

Use cookware marked induction-compatible; a magnet should stick to the base.

fixSteps.title: Check cookware
fixSteps.instruction: Hold a magnet to pan base; it should stick firmly.

whenToCallPro: If compatible pans still fail to detect.
videoSearchQuery: Frigidaire induction F9 pan detection fix

faq.a: Cast iron and magnetic stainless steel.

title: Runaway Element Detection
shortDescription: An element is heating without being commanded.
fullDescription:
F10 is triggered when the control detects an element drawing power despite being off, typically due to a welded relay.

This is a safety shutdown — do not use the cooktop until repaired.

fixSteps.title: Replace control board
fixSteps.instruction: Swap main control or affected relay board.

whenToCallPro: Strongly recommended due to safety risk.
videoSearchQuery: Frigidaire cooktop F10 runaway element fix

faq.a: Yes — keep breaker off until repaired.

title: Stuck Key Detected
shortDescription: A control key appears pressed for too long.
fullDescription:
F11 is flagged when a touch key or mechanical knob reports continuous input for more than 60 seconds. The control locks out to prevent unintended heating.

Clean the surface, ensure nothing rests on the controls, and power cycle.

fixSteps.title: Remove items
fixSteps.instruction: Clear all objects from the control surface.

fixSteps.title: Replace UI board
fixSteps.instruction: If issue persists, install new user interface module.

videoSearchQuery: Frigidaire cooktop F11 stuck key fix

faq.a: The alarm indicates prolonged key activation.
